title: 4.1.6 import memory control: ownership, progress, byte batching and spill
authorization: User requests all remaining memory-control fixes and CSV alignment; online resizing and non-glibc platforms excluded.

design_gate.trigger: Crosses allocation, operator, spill-file and compiler ownership; adds cancellable admission coordination and shared spill-source lifecycle. Design-first required by mo-dev.

problem_evidence: Stock first complete import succeeds and second fails under 22 GiB; idle writer capacity and allocator resident free pages contribute to history dependence.

V2 closes one cleanup leak, bounds idle Arena bytes and adds native trim; five uninterrupted 39-table rounds pass, but review identifies impossible-admission, reclaim-threshold-gap, retained-delete reservation and incomplete upstream bounds.
Per-writer 20 ms ForceRefresh causes redundant process sampling/reclaim and has no fairness guarantee.
CSV currently limits raw input field bytes; MultiUpdate projections and vector capacities can amplify the next allocation.
HashBuild spills only shuffle, copies before testing the threshold; scatter buffers are row bounded and max-depth skew reload is unbounded.
goals: The tested amway import semantics, indexes, row counts and SQL success remain intact under fixed 22 GiB and no inter-round idle/GC/restart.
Every satisfiable admission wait is driven by owner release or reclaim, not an independent 20 ms polling loop.
Every large import-owned buffer retains a budget charge until destruction or a documented transfer.
Normal writer reuse and asynchronous IO are preserved where budgets permit.
Input and spill frames are bounded by actual typed bytes, not only rows or raw CSV bytes.
Broadcast and skew spill produce complete join semantics without unbounded reload.
exclusions: Adding native trim support for non-glibc systems
Remote publication or release without existing authorization
Guaranteeing success when a single irreducible row or minimum query working set cannot fit the environment, or external allocations consume the entire shared cgroup

Providing a finite working-set guarantee for arbitrary variable-length SQL function expansion without a pre-evaluation capacity contract; these statements retain legacy execution, including the existing unrestricted skew fallback where applicable.

invariants.Q1: Each reservation, workspace, owned buffer and spill FD has exactly one effective terminal owner; transfer keeps the charge/source alive until the consumer releases it.
invariants.Q2: A task cannot wait for normal data credits while holding the only workspace that is needed to free those data credits. Reclaim and cancellation never depend on the blocked writer.
invariants.Q3: Input batch, private retained capacity, pending jobs, spill bucket buffers, spill frames and skew working sets have byte bounds. A cache limit alone is not an active-memory limit.
invariants.accounting: Use per-owner allocated capacity, not cumulative processed input. Go and native pool allocations both count; serialization/map/bitmap state has an explicit capacity charge.
invariants.progress: Too-large requests are split before waiting. Physical-pressure denial drives one merged reclaim+fresh sample even below the RSS soft line. Pool denial waits for actual ownership release.
invariants.performance: No per-writer periodic sampling; hot-path accounting reuses atomic counters and row-window boundaries, with no full retained-state scan for every row.

decisions.choice: Retain nonblocking RSCThrottler compatibility; add optional cancellable admission, request-size and byte-unit capabilities.
decisions.rationale: Existing mocks and nonblocking spill decisions remain compatible.

decisions.choice: FIFO notification-driven waits with a single process coordinator and a one-second fallback only while waiters exist.
decisions.rationale: Release/reclaim events wake immediately; fallback observes external frees without 50*N process samples per second. A queued request cannot be bypassed by new ordinary grants.

decisions.choice: Native/process reclamation is single flight and cancellation-independent; denied physical admission may request reclaim below 85% RSS.
decisions.rationale: Closes the confirmed 17+6>22 GiB threshold gap without lowering a magic percentage.

decisions.choice: Calibrate physical pressure using process RSS and same-cgroup usage after separating reclaimable inactive file cache; do not add RSS and cgroup usage.
decisions.rationale: The signals overlap and must not be double counted. Keep raw cgroup usage observable.

decisions.choice: Released grants lose their old RSS-covered credit; reclaimable libc pages count as resident until a fresh sample proves they returned.
decisions.rationale: Cross-arena free chunks are not guaranteed headroom for a new owner.

decisions.choice: Use one byte-unit policy for CSV, writer subbatches and spill frames. CSV enforces raw and typed capacity bounds; MultiUpdate rechecks all actual projections.
decisions.rationale: CSV cannot infer every downstream index projection. Varlen windows must count referenced payload rather than their shared entire area.

decisions.choice: MultiUpdate uses a private accounting mpool and an owned-capacity counter that includes Go and native buffers; all retained delete/index metadata remain charged.
decisions.rationale: A shared process mpool delta cannot identify this writer's ownership, especially with async jobs.

decisions.choice: Separate ordinary retained data grants from a bounded process IO/spill workspace permit. A spill/IO worker never waits for ordinary data grants held by its submitter.
decisions.rationale: Prevents the main-Sync to worker-budget wait cycle. Workspace is acquired before writing and transferred with jobs, then released on success/error/cancel.

decisions.choice: Before mutation reserve a conservative computed append/serialization growth envelope; after the operation reconcile to actual retained capacity.
decisions.rationale: Accounting only after allocation cannot bound a temporary resize/clone peak. Envelope derives from vector growth and encoded/compression sizes, not customer data names.

decisions.choice: Keep total idle Arena byte cap, but share its budget across size tiers on demand.
decisions.rationale: A tier cannot discard useful buffers while the other tier leaves budget unused. Checked-out ownership remains separate from idle cache.

decisions.choice: HashBuild requests retained-data budget before copying; denial starts spill using the reserved IO workspace.
decisions.rationale: No build operator holds its data waiting for a downstream writer to free memory.

decisions.choice: Broadcast spill retains a shared immutable build source. Probe streams spool bounded files; after all participants register, a single spill consumer owns combined probe sources and executes the existing join semantics.
decisions.rationale: Preserves right/full/semi/anti/single matching without incompatible per-probe bitmaps or an on-the-fly shuffle protocol. Only the spill path serializes; normal broadcast parallelism stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: Skew fallback at the recursion bound uses bounded build chunks and replays probe data, with disk sidecar match state where needed.
decisions.rationale: All-equal keys cannot be fixed by more repartitioning. Preserve LEFT/FULL/SEMI/ANTI/SINGLE cross-chunk match semantics without loading the entire bucket.

decisions.choice: Serialize spill frames without a second unbounded whole-batch copy; limit scatter by aggregate bytes across buckets before Union.
decisions.rationale: Spilling must not reproduce the original wide-row memory peak.

decisions.choice: Enable statement working sets only for whole-DAG bounded CSV/JSONLINE sources and join-key expression contracts supported before evaluation. Column keys, fixed-width expressions and bounded serial/composite keys share one capacity derivation for normal hash, spill and skew. Unknown variable-length expression expansion retains whole-query legacy execution.
decisions.rationale: The CSV raw-record limit does not bound generic table scans or arbitrary expression expansion. Fallback must preserve legal query semantics and cannot advertise unbounded operators as admitted memory.

decisions.choice: Control streams use a separate backend pool and caller context during backend acquisition. Returned stream lifetime remains explicit and independent. Board cleanup occurs only after closed root plus final attached scope cleanup.
decisions.rationale: A control owner must not consume the last execution connection, and cancelling a scope does not prove it has stopped reading shared buffers.

decisions.choice: Probe process-instance UUID with admission capability. If a statement includes multiple CNs sharing one process coordinator, use whole-query legacy. Otherwise acquire in (process UUID,CN UUID) order and validate expected process UUID before every Open/Reserve.
decisions.rationale: CN ordering is insufficient when distinct CN identities alias one process coordinator: one statement can self-wait, and two statements can introduce opposite physical-process edges through different CN aliases. An Open epoch check prevents a restart after capability discovery from changing the ordering identity.

decisions.choice: Use the early irregular-index source only for FAIL/ordinary LOAD. IGNORE maintenance consumes a final projection downstream of duplicate filtering, with or without regular indexes. UPDATE also consumes final images and alone emits old-index deletes.
decisions.rationale: Public SQL showed ignored duplicate-PK text leaking into FT while the base row and BTREE remained correct after the UPDATE-only guard. The original mixed-index code accidentally restored the filtered source; retain correct IGNORE filtering without recreating the unnecessary ordinary-LOAD old-table join.

alternatives.name: Tune current percentages/timers only
alternatives.rejected: Does not close impossible requests, mismatched reclaim thresholds, owner accounting or no-workspace cycles.

alternatives.name: Convert all broadcast joins to shuffle
alternatives.rejected: SINGLE and right-oriented semantics/topology are not uniformly supported; normal small-query parallelism and data routing change.

alternatives.name: Per-probe independent broadcast spill readers
alternatives.rejected: Independent repartitioning invalidates shared build-row bitmap/finalization for right/full variants.

alternatives.name: One global callback for every allocation with blocking acquisition
alternatives.rejected: Can block while an allocation owner holds resources needed by its own spill/cleanup. Hot-path overhead and partial mutation retry semantics are unacceptable.

throttler.max_policy: CN max derives from the existing acquire policy; do not duplicate 0.8 in callers.
throttler.wait_protocol: Subscribe/enqueue before recheck, Release and dequeue share queue synchronization; cancellation removes its node and wakes successor; last waiter shuts down fallback.
throttler.reclaim_protocol: Acquire denial reason selects owner-release wait vs process reclaim. Reclaim IO/callbacks occur outside queue locks.

owned_mpool.meaning: Current allocation capacity belonging to this pool, Go and native; existing offheap-only public stats retain their semantics.
owned_mpool.terminal_rule: AllocatedBytes decrements after actual Free/deallocation, not before. Same-pool native Realloc updates capacity in one atomic delta. Pool registration removal does not erase a live transferred-buffer counter.

csv.semantics: Keep raw line and row limits, additionally bound typed capacity to shared byte unit; a crossing row is retained safely without reusing parser backing storage. Open/Close/EOF/error/reset clear pending state.
csv.accounting: Source batch storage and one crossing-row working set must be represented in the query/import working budget; no unlimited pending-row queue.
csv.copy_boundary: Both UnionAll pre-growth and UnionBatch whole-area fast path must use compact referenced payload; shared-window full backing area cannot bypass the admitted byte window.

writer.charge: private mpool + retained Go capacities/maps/bitmaps + assigned file scratch/workspace; async job source and workspace transfer together.
writer.failures: Partial append/write/Sync errors propagate normal errors; temporary quota denial is handled internally without SQL failure or duplicate publication.

workspace.bound: One process budget, bounded bytes and simultaneous permits; IO has reserved capacity that ordinary retained data cannot consume.
workspace.progress: Holder must complete IO/cancel without acquiring normal data grants. No task waiting for a workspace may be the only owner that can release that same workspace.
workspace.minimum: Byte unit is reduced to fit the environment; one irreducible row/minimum working set must fit. Query/import admission must account for source and required operator workspace before normal data fills the available headroom.

broadcast_spill.source: JoinMap owns immutable build FDs and a participant-scoped spill handoff; source closes after final owner. Per-reader logical offsets use ReadAt/SectionReader, never dup+shared Seek.
broadcast_spill.handoff: Each expected probe registers its bounded probe files exactly once, including empty input. The last registrant takes combined work; other probes end. Cancellation aborts coordination and closes unclaimed files.
broadcast_spill.finalize: The consumer runs with one logical finalizer so RIGHT/FULL and directional semi/anti/single matching retain existing semantics.
broadcast_spill.normal_path: No handoff/coordinator is created when the build stays in memory.

skew_fallback.state: Current build chunk only in RAM; probe match sidecar persists across chunk replays; output unmatched probe only after final chunk. Scalar SINGLE detects second match across all chunks using existing SQL error semantics.
skew_fallback.cost: Worst-case IO may be buildChunks times probeBytes; this is an explicit bounded-memory degradation, not a zero-overhead claim.

roles.I: Fixed per-pipeline input/output storage and parser credit, owned until consumption; cannot be borrowed by D/W.
roles.D: Ordinary retained capacity; acquire complete new allocation before mutation; denial causes flush/spill.
roles.W: One process execution slot for destructible spill/encode/IO workspace. Queued jobs hold no slot; no W holder requests D or another W.

working_set_protocol.entry: Compile.prePipelineInitializer before execution locks and InitAllDataSource. Nested execution must inherit a compatible ticket or reserve before parent locks; no hidden recursive admission.
working_set_protocol.topology: Use maximum effective local Scope Mcpu and every independent live input/output stage, including nested/async stages. This is a conservative planning bound; actual broadcast IDs are separately sealed after duplication.
working_set_protocol.I_promise: sum of all live tickets input-slot bytes, including returned output until downstream consumes it
working_set_protocol.W_promise: max(IOBytes of live tickets); exactly one process W job executes
working_set_protocol.atomic: Reserve I increment plus any increase in W maximum atomically before publishing ticket. Reduce target unit and recompute schema envelopes if statically unsatisfiable; a first-admission waiter owns no execution locks or data.
working_set_protocol.unit: min(64 MiB, admissible request unit), reducible before execution. Target is not a new single-row limit.
working_set_protocol.lifetime: Root, active input, queued IO and transferred job hold references. Close cancels queued acquisition and drops root; active jobs remain valid. Final owner removes promises and recomputes W maximum.
working_set_protocol.output: A W job can publish only into a pre-reserved output I slot or transfer an existing D owner without additional blocking allocation. Returned output cannot keep the only W slot while downstream needs W.
working_set_protocol.zero_D: A legal input window borrowed from I can directly spill through W with D full; no clone into D first.
working_set_protocol.physical: U=max(RSS,max(0,cgroupCurrent-inactiveFile)); predicted use adds outstanding I/W/D promises and proposed increase, minus only proven live resident coverage. Default coverage is zero. Raw cgroup current remains observable. This conservatively overcounts resident allocations; performance must be measured.
working_set_protocol.coordination: One process coordinator coalesces sampling/reclaim across throttlers. Denial below RSS soft threshold still requests reclaim. Release wakes immediately. One-second fallback only with waiters. Ordinary FIFO cannot block W.

source_and_writer_revision.capacity: MPool.AllocatedBytes counts current Go and native allocated capacity. Global public offheap stats retain existing meaning. Private pool lives until all transferred buffers free.
source_and_writer_revision.growth: If required exceeds old capacity O, reserve complete new capacity N while O remains charged; never reserve only N-O. Reuse precise vector/mpool growth rules.
source_and_writer_revision.payload: Window byte accounting counts referenced out-of-line varlen payload, inline/null/const semantics and every actual projection; Window.Size is not the bound.
source_and_writer_revision.source_envelope: Q=max(unit,TypedRowUpperBound(configured rawRowLimit,schema)). Include typed old plus complete new capacity, raw record old/new growth, readUntil scratch, unescape/charset temporary storage, fixed parser block and field metadata. SourceEnvelope is calculated from this concrete allocation table.
source_and_writer_revision.raw_limit: Use the existing configured txn-entry-size-limit support boundary, with no new 64MiB row limit. Inspect parser semantics and prevent complete-record/field-metadata growth bypass before allocation; document compatibility of any corrected bypass.
csv_states: read raw row into parser backing view
before vector mutation compute typed demand and full new capacity
if nonempty batch crosses unit return batch and preserve one pending raw view without reading parser again
singleton above target is allowed within reserved row envelope
EOF/error/Open/Close/reset retire pending and parser state
source_and_writer_revision.io_envelope: IOEnvelope shares implementation-owned sizing functions for sort/merge output, serializer full new capacity, compression bound and allocation rounding, arena fallback, object/block metadata. Borrowed source I/D is excluded; existing and new scratch coexist in W.
source_and_writer_revision.preextend: PreExtend uses the admitted byte-window row count rather than unconditional 8192 rows.
source_and_writer_revision.writer: Private pool plus manual map/bitmap/capacity ownership is reconciled after mutation. Automatic spill only returns destroyed/transferred capacity; freeList and uncommitted delete stay charged.
source_and_writer_revision.eval: Stream per-writer output instead of out.Append through proc.Mp. Metadata is framed/drained during Build or spooled in bounded frames so a single writer cannot grow unlimited metadata before Eval. Preserve MergeBlock transaction semantics.
source_and_writer_revision.async: Acquire W before executing, transfer with job; queued jobs own input references but no W. Sync may wait for job; job cannot request D/second W. Error/cancel follow same final-owner cleanup.

hashbuild_revision.precopy: Reserve full new vector capacity before copy. Nonblocking denial starts spill with W; no retained-data wait.
hashbuild_revision.prehash: Capacity calculation lives with hashmap allocator and includes load-factor rounding, old+new resize peak, Sels/results/offsets, key-expression/unique-key scratch and iterator/output storage. Use worst row count and checked arithmetic.
hashbuild_revision.denial: Preserve original batches; destroy unpublished partial hashmap; spill original rows; release only destroyed D. Subsequent input spills directly.
hashbuild_revision.publish: Batches, hashmap, Sels and their D leases transfer together to JoinMap and survive until last probe; NeedBatches=false releases only destroyed owners.

broadcast_spill_revision.topology: Each CN probe scope receives stable SpillScopeID; SpillExpectedScopes enumerates its complete per-CN group. Scope duplication seals only its own actual ParallelIDs before Prepare. Composite participant=(scopeID<<32)|parallelID. Build may publish before all scopes seal. Claim requires all expected scopes sealed and all actual participants registered. MessageBoard registry rebuilds the shared local group by JoinMapTag and query epoch across remote scope RPCs.
broadcast_spill_revision.register: Each probe spools bounded private input, including empty stream, releases local W, then registers exactly once. Last participant atomically claims all probe files and immutable build source. Others end without waiting.
broadcast_spill_revision.failure: Registration before-error/IO/cancel/failed Reset aborts epoch. Query-context independent cleanup covers never-started participants. Lock protects ownership transfer only; no IO/allocation/FD-close under coordinator lock.
broadcast_spill_revision.abort: Collecting abort detaches registered files and closes outside lock; unregistered remain local. Claimed abort cancels consumer but never closes its active FD concurrently. Claim/Abort linearize to exactly one terminal owner.
broadcast_spill_revision.bitmap: All probes consult shared spill-generation state, including Reset before JoinMap receive. Spill generation sends/waits on no old bitmapChannel. Claimant executes one logical finalizer; normal in-memory protocol stays unchanged.
broadcast_spill_revision.source: Immutable source and each reader have references. SectionReader/ReadAt gives independent logical offsets; dup plus Seek is forbidden. Source closes only after last source/reader reference.
broadcast_spill_revision.bucket: Every FD explicitly local/queued/active. Pop establishes active ownership before reader creation. Repartition publishes children only after successful completion; all failures close local/active/queued resources exactly once.

spill_codec_revision.compatibility: Original buffer API delegates the common implementation and retains byte-for-byte persistent format. Temporary spill framing uses bounded counting writer and header patching with WriteAt.
spill_codec_revision.framing: No whole-batch serialized copy. Only complete frames are published. Short write, malformed/oversized lengths and encode errors terminate and clean owner.
spill_codec_revision.scatter: All buckets share aggregate byte budget. Flush/shrink before Union or PreExtend. Shared varlen area is compacted into bounded window before serialization; stream API alone is insufficient.

skew_fallback_revision.mode: At max repartition depth, bounded build chunks replay probe files. Never ignore budget and load entire bucket.
skew_fallback_revision.probe_ids: Stable ParticipantID plus local row ordinal survives repartition. Sealed participant prefix yields global probe ID.
skew_fallback_revision.sidecar: Disk-backed match counts/state with bounded page cache, no whole-state RAM bitmap/mmap residency. File bytes/cache/FD count recorded.

semantics.INNER: emit each matching pair once per chunk
semantics.LEFT: pairs per chunk; unmatched probe only after all chunks
semantics.RIGHT: pairs; unmatched build after all probe sources for current chunk
semantics.FULL: RIGHT chunk finalization plus LEFT final probe scan
semantics.LEFT_SEMI: emit only first transition to matched
semantics.LEFT_ANTI: emit unmatched probe after all chunks
semantics.RIGHT_SEMI: emit matched build once at current chunk finalization
semantics.RIGHT_ANTI: emit unmatched build at current chunk finalization
semantics.LEFT_SINGLE: count across chunks, second complete match errors with existing semantics; unmatched after all chunks
semantics.RIGHT_SINGLE: count across all probes for current build row, second match errors; unmatched at chunk finalization

skew_fallback_revision.conditions: Use original equality, NULL and additional non-equality predicates before recording match.
skew_fallback_revision.cursor: Persist bucket, chunk, participant/file/frame/row, match-list offset, build-finalize row, final probe scan and phase across Call. Advance cursor and sidecar before returning output. IO errors terminate rather than replay already-published output. Empty chunk advances source.
skew_fallback_revision.cost: Worst-case IO is build-chunks times probe bytes; acceptance measures this bounded-memory degradation.

remote_execution.entry: Remote decodeScope executes MergeRun without Compile.prePipelineInitializer; admit and attach the local working set and initialize local spill registry before reader/source initialization there, with identical final cleanup.
remote_execution.backward_compatibility: New readers without topology fields keep broadcast builds in memory. Old binaries ignore unknown fields and retain their existing in-memory broadcast path. Every build and all its probe scopes share a CN binary; FDs never cross CN/process/version. Existing shuffle path remains supported.
remote_execution.scope: Narrow extension of pipeline metadata only; no persistent/catalog/SQL protocol format change.

whole_query_admission.manifest: Origin enumerates the complete scope DAG per CN, carrying stage schema/role/retained-field/concurrency descriptors plus statement epoch and incoming frame unit; remote recomputes envelopes using its local configuration. Every scope RPC carries only the token/reference to this same complete local ticket.
whole_query_admission.ordering: Before any execution locks, reads or retained allocation, origin opens/reserves all participating CNs including itself in stable CN UUID order. Every query uses this order. Partial success is registered for cleanup immediately. DOP recompilation releases every partial ticket before rebuilding.
whole_query_admission.commit: After every CN admits, commit the minimum selected target unit to all CNs. Promise size may shrink, never increase. Receiver input slots still cover the incoming frame bound. Only then execute any pipeline.
whole_query_admission.owner: One dedicated statement admission control stream per remote CN owns the MessageBoard root ticket. Scope RPCs attach/detach references; normal scope cancellation cannot close or abort the shared root. Scope-start and Close are linearized; an absent/closed token is rejected, never recreated.
whole_query_admission.termination: After all remote scopes/notifications join, origin sends END or ABORT with a cleanup context independent of the cancelled query. An acknowledged END permits ordinary stream close. Any failed send/ack/control-context forces Close(true) on the exclusively locked backend, so server SessionCtx.Done runs root cleanup even if END is lost. Server handler defer removes token, closes root and cancels attached unfinished scopes. No forever tombstone or expected-RPC-count cleanup.
tests: Two origins acquire CNs in opposite natural orders; stable global order prevents wait cycle
Build map stays live while late probe RPC attaches without requesting new I/W
Cancellation before all CNs admit releases partial tickets
END lost or send/ack failure closes independent backend and retires ticket/FDs
Single normal scope cancellation leaves other scopes shared ticket valid
Late attach after root Close is rejected without resurrection

planner_action_fix.classification: Focused ordinary planner bug, design document exemption; recorded here because it changes the acceptance plan.
planner_action_fix.contract: Only UPDATE action records old irregular-index deletion. Plain INSERT/LOAD and IGNORE retain their new-row index maintenance source when regular index projections are appended.
planner_action_fix.evidence: TestInsertIrregularMaintenanceAction fails insert/ignore on the original source, passes ODKU; with action guard all three pass. Real SQL index correctness is required.

component_contracts.control_terminal: Control close marks closed/removes token/cancels scopes/closes root WS; shared MessageBoard cleanup waits until all attached scopes detach after operator cleanup. Repeated identical Commit is read-only after publication.
component_contracts.control_transport: Dedicated optional ControlStreamClient uses a separate backend pool, owned/closed by the pipeline client; a control stream cannot occupy the last execution backend. Caller context controls only backend creation/acquisition; returned stream lifetime is independently closed. Existing disconnected server SessionCtx retires on the shared 10s morpc sweep.
component_contracts.expression_key_wire: After eligibility is proved on the full AST, both join-key sides and non-equality predicate are protobuf-marshaled into manifest byte fields; receivers unmarshal without evaluating and derive the same expression capacity. Unknown function allocation contracts and non-NULL varlen literals retain whole-query legacy. Fixed results alone are not a scratch bound; only audited primitive kernels and serial/serial_full are supported.
component_contracts.distributed_unit: All CNs Open before execution, then Commit the global minimum UnitBytes. Therefore each receiver frame is no larger than that receiver own admitted unit (or its already budgeted legal singleton); origin manifests set IncomingUnit=0. Capacity-expression overflow at a large target may shrink unit and retry; malformed descriptors do not.
component_contracts.process_alias: common/runtime.ProcessInstanceID is generated once per process, not per service. GetProtocolVersionResponse optional field3 carries it. Missing process identity retains legacy. Same-process multi-CN is conservatively compatible through legacy; physical manifest merging is outside this fix.

ownership_and_wait_graphs: CSV parser -> owned typed input batch -> downstream read-only view; source storage released/reused only after downstream consumption.
Writer private pool -> Sinker/free-list or output metadata -> synchronous cleanup or transferred consumer; matching grant survives transfer.
Writer -> pending IO job -> source batches + workspace -> job terminal cleanup; writer Sync waits job but job does not wait writer normal quota.
HashBuild retained lease -> in-memory JoinMap -> last probe ref -> pool+grant release.
HashBuild spill files -> immutable shared source -> probe handoff consumer -> bucket/chunk readers -> terminal close.
Waiting admission -> Release or merged reclaim sample or fallback -> recheck; context cancellation independently removes waiter.

compatibility.wire: Backward-compatible optional pipeline topology fields identify per-CN broadcast spill participants. Missing topology disables new broadcast spill. No SQL protocol or cross-CN FD transfer.
compatibility.persistence: Only anonymous temporary spill framing may change; no persistent object/catalog format change.
compatibility.upgrade: New queries use one process binary. No cross-version temporary FD sharing is introduced.
compatibility.scope: Enable the new working-set admission only when the complete physical DAG has a controlled CSV/JSONLINE source. Generic SELECT/UPDATE/table scans lack this raw-row/typed-batch contract and retain the legacy path; already admitted remote tokens remain valid on a CN without a source.
compatibility.capability_probe: GetProtocolVersionResponse optional bool memory_admission=2; old peers omit it. Probe all CNs before Open; any false uses whole-query legacy, network errors fail normally. Legacy pipeline StopSending does not ACK and cannot be used for probing.
compatibility.legacy_skew: Without ImportMemory, every max-depth shuffle preserves the prior whole-bucket path. No new default 64MiB singleton limit is imposed on ordinary SELECT/UPDATE or unsupported function-key imports.

unit: Impossible request split without permanent wait
17+6>22 physical denial triggers reclaim below soft line
FIFO release wakeup, cancellation and no lost notifications
Last waiter stops shared fallback and no background worker without waiters
Actual capacity balance including native/Go realloc and cross-pool free
Retained uncommitted delete and metadata stay charged
Multi-owner/index publication exactly once across subbatches
CSV typed expansion, varlen shared area, pending row EOF/reset/cancel
Shared cache budget conservation under concurrent get/put/drain
Broadcast two or more probes with interleaved source lifetime and one finalizer
Skew at max depth for all supported join modes, NULL and non-equi conditions
Spill/IO memory peak and cancellation without main-worker quota cycles
Complete working-set atomic admission and final reference rollback
D full: input parses and direct spills via independent W
Two queued jobs: only runner holds W; Sync cannot form a D/W wait cycle
Typed and raw CSV capacity checks happen before growth
Actual duplicated topology seals IDs and retires old bitmap reset protocol
All join variants compared to independent multiset oracle with one-row Call outputs
Short write and frame decode failure close active/queued/source FDs
validation.negative_controls: Each repaired contract must have a discriminating old-code or disabled-mechanism oracle; do not accept compile errors as negative proof.
validation.race: Focused adaptive race per changed concurrency test plus affected owning packages once.
validation.public_consumer: SQL checks with forced-small budgets/spill, main and index counts plus join multiset oracles; native fixed 39-table amway imports.
validation.real_import: Same CSV/DDL/SQL/order, 22 GiB no swap, no deliberate gap/GC/restart between at least five rounds; process remains alive after trial.
validation.performance: Record full/table wall time, RSS+cgroup peaks, allocated capacity, spill bytes/objects, native reclaim count and wait samples. Compare stock successful 303.1-second round and V2 mean 331.1 seconds; do not declare zero regression from shared-host variation.

phases: Shared throttler/accounting/workspace primitives with deterministic tests

delivery.publication: No push/PR/release in this design step.
